title: Coaching inside a group session
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainers and instructors who lead group sessions
learningOutcomes: Pre-plan a group session with a modification for each member
Apply a coaching rhythm that gives each member frequent, brief attention
Stop or modify an exercise when a member reports warning symptoms, and follow the referral route

instruction.heading: Plan each member before the session
instruction.body: Before the session, read each member's notes and write their modification for the main exercises. A written plan keeps your attention on people instead of the next exercise. Include the member's current goal and any limitation flagged at screening. The plan is a set of starting points, to be adjusted when a member's day goes differently.

instruction.heading: Use a short, regular coaching rhythm
instruction.body: A simple rule helps. When you pass a member, watch for about three repetitions, then give one correction or one encouraging comment and move on. Over a session, every member should get frequent contact. Members who feel ignored often leave without saying why. Apply the rule the same way across the group.

instruction.heading: Keep effort within safe limits
instruction.body: The aim is effort the member can sustain with good form, not effort that matches the fittest person in the room. Watch for changes in form, breathing or colour, and for any report of pain, dizziness or chest discomfort. Stop the exercise, follow your emergency procedure and the referral route, and record the event. Screening and emergency response are covered in the screening and supervision lessons and are not repeated here.

procedure: Read each member's notes and write one modification per main exercise before the session.
Run the warm-up and check each member performs it with good form.
Coach with the rhythm: watch, correct or encourage, move on.
Check the flagged-limitation list at the start of each block.
For any warning sign, stop, follow the escalation route, and record it.

workedExamples.situation: A hypothetical member with a sore knee joins a group lunge set.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the trainer do during the set?
workedExamples.reasoning: The trainer uses the supported split-squat variation chosen in the plan, watches the knee and form, and stops that exercise if pain increases. The member is not asked to match the group. The change and the observation go into the session notes.

equipmentAndPpe: First-aid kit and emergency contact sheet (see the supervision lesson)

commonErrors.error: Leaving a member unsupervised through a long set
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the rhythm and rotate attention across the group.

commonErrors.error: Pushing a member to match the group
commonErrors.prevention: Set effort from the member's plan, not the group's.

commonErrors.error: Continuing an exercise after a warning sign

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Emergency response, supervision and first aid are covered in the supervision lesson. This lesson does not set supervision requirements.
Check screening of minors and any child-safety requirements in the screening lesson for the course.
This lesson does not grant a qualification and does not allow the trainer to diagnose or treat any condition.

qualityStandard: Each member has a written modification for the main exercises
Coaching contact is spread across the group during every block
Every warning sign is stopped, escalated and recorded
documentationEvidence: Incident note for any warning sign
summary: Plan each member before the session.
Coach in short, regular contacts across the group.
Stop and escalate on any warning sign.

knowledgeChecks.question: The three-repetition rule in this lesson means the trainer:
options: Watches each member for about three repetitions, gives a correction or comment, then moves on
Counts three sets for each member and checks the plan for each member in the group before moving on
Stops the session after three minutes and then sends everyone home early for the day

knowledgeChecks.question: Planning ahead helps a group trainer mainly by:
options: Removing the need for notes and the need for any plan at all
Setting modifications for each member before the session starts
Replacing the warm-up with a longer cool-down for every member

knowledgeChecks.question: A member reports increasing pain during a group exercise. The correct response is:
options: Push through to keep pace with the group and do not mention the pain to anyone
Stop or modify the exercise and follow the escalation and referral route
Record it and continue unchanged and tell nobody in the group about it
